text: Inauspicious means pointing toward a bad outcome, the opposite of auspicious, which signals good luck. The word goes back to Roman priests who read the flight of birds for omens. Mr Trump's record-low approval was an inauspicious sign for Republicans.
A drubbing is a crushing, one-sided defeat, as if the loser had been thrashed with a stick. Here it describes how badly Republicans lost, much as under George W. Bush in 2006.
Fealty is a pledge of loyalty to a leader, originally a knight's vow to his lord. Republicans who swore fealty to Mr Trump now must decide whether that loyalty is still worth it.
Midterm elections take place halfway through a president's four-year term. The president is not on the ballot, so they work like a report card on his performance, and his party usually loses seats.
Net approval is the share of people who approve of a leader minus the share who disapprove. A negative number means more people disapprove than approve.
The out-of-power party is the one that does not hold the presidency. Its voters are often more eager to turn out in a midterm, which is why it tends to gain seats.
A wipeout is a total defeat, borrowed from surfing, where a wave knocks a rider off the board. Here it means Republicans did far worse than expected.
The popular vote is the total number of votes cast across the whole country, regardless of how they are split among districts or states. A party can win the popular vote yet still win fewer seats.
The House of Representatives is the larger chamber of Congress, with 435 members, each representing one district. All of them face election every two years.
A percentage point is the gap between two percentages. If one party gets 53% and the other 40%, the lead is 13 percentage points, which is not the same as a 13% lead.
A polling average combines many opinion polls into one number, which smooths out the errors of any single poll. Democrats did about four points better than that average predicted.
A landslide is literally a mass of earth sliding down a hill. In politics it means a victory by an overwhelming margin.
The Senate has 100 members, two per state, serving six-year terms. A majority of 51 lets a party control which bills and appointments move forward. It is called the upper chamber.
A stronghold is a place where one side is overwhelmingly strong. Republican strongholds are states, like Texas or Ohio, where Republicans normally win easily.
Eye-popping describes something so large or surprising that it makes you stare. Here it describes huge winning margins.
Blue is the colour American media uses for Democrats, red for Republicans. A tsunami is a giant wave, so a blue tsunami is a huge Democratic surge.
Drenched means soaked through. Continuing the water image of a tsunami, it says Democratic gains reached House and governor races, not just the Senate.
Gubernatorial means having to do with a governor, the elected head of a US state.
To flip a seat is to win it from the other party. A flipped governor's mansion means the office changed party.
Each state's governor lives in an official residence called the governor's mansion. The phrase stands for the governorship itself.
Forbidding usually describes something that looks unfriendly or threatening. Here the Senate map looked tough, meaning few Democratic pickups seemed possible.
The electoral map is the set of states and districts up for election and which party leans where. In 2026 it favoured Republicans, but the national mood outweighed it.
Double digits means a margin of ten or more points. A state Mr Trump won by double digits was not close.
To barrel into something is to rush into it recklessly, like a heavy barrel rolling downhill. The article says Mr Trump plunged into a conflict with Iran.
A trade war is a fight between countries in which each raises taxes (tariffs) on the other's goods. It tends to raise prices for shoppers.
Recall can mean remember, but when a thing recalls another, it reminds you of it. Mr Trump's defeat resembles Bush's in 2006.
The Iraq war began in 2003 under George W. Bush and grew unpopular, helping Democrats win both chambers of Congress in 2006.
To be fired up is to be full of energy and eager to act. Fired-up voters turn out in larger numbers.
Independents are voters who do not belong to either major party. They often decide close elections, so losing them hurts.
An incumbent is the person currently holding an office. Incumbents usually have an advantage, so losing the party's backing is unusual.
To concoct is to put together, often something unlikely. Candidates concocted from Democrats' fever dreams means they seemed made to order for the other side.
A fever dream is a strange, vivid dream had when ill. Here it means a wild wish or imagining, in this case Democratic strategists' ideal opponents.
To sue is to take someone to court to demand compensation or justice.
A swing is a shift in votes from one party to another between elections. A heavy swing towards Democrats means many voters changed sides.
To shore up is to strengthen something that is weak, like propping up a sagging wall.
Gerrymandering is drawing district boundaries to favour one party. Mid-decade means doing it between the usual once-every-ten-years redraws.
A spree is a short burst of doing one thing without restraint, like a shopping spree.
To hold means to continue. Republicans bet that their gains among Hispanic voters would hold, meaning last.
A county is a subdivision of a US state. Election results are often compared county by county.
Staggering means so large it almost knocks you off balance. A 47-point win is astonishingly big.
Reversion is a return to an earlier state. The Hispanic vote reverting means it went back to its earlier Democratic lean.
To nullify is to cancel the effect of something. The redistricting plan barely achieved what it was designed to do.
A gerrymandered district has boundaries drawn to favour one party, so a Democratic win there is a sign of how large the swing was.
Turnout is the share of eligible people who actually vote.
To tout is to promote something loudly. Republicans had little good news to tout.
Diesel is a fuel used by trucks, tractors and trains. Its price affects the cost of moving food and goods.
A mortgage is a loan to buy a home, and the mortgage rate is its interest. Higher rates make homes more expensive each month.
When prices rise faster than pay, people can buy less than before, even though their paychecks are bigger.
Tariffs are taxes on imported goods. They can raise prices and prompt other countries to retaliate, which hurt farmers who sell abroad.
The social safety net is the set of programmes, like food aid and health insurance, that help people in hardship.
Deportation is forcing non-citizens to leave the country. A mass-deportation campaign does this on a large scale.
Fear-mongering is deliberately stirring up fear to win support.
Wokery is a mocking term used by critics for progressive attitudes on social issues. It shows what some Republican candidates campaigned against.
A jihadist is a violent Islamist extremist. Calling a political opponent one is a very serious, inflammatory charge.
A president can veto a bill, but Congress can override that with two-thirds of both chambers. A party with such a majority is veto-proof. Democrats lack it.
To herald is to announce or signal the arrival of something. The election does not herald a new era of lawmaking.
Unequivocal means clear, with no room for doubt.
A headlock is a wrestling hold gripping someone's head. To have a party in a headlock means controlling it tightly.
A primary is an election within a party to choose its candidate for the main election. A president who is angry at a politician can back a rival in that primary.
To cling is to hold on tightly. Republicans who cling to Mr Trump could lose in the general election.
The general election is the contest between the parties' nominees, held after the primaries.
